content: 1. Childhood vaccinations should ideally be administered prior to initiating myeloablative conditioning. 2. The quadrivalent intranasal influenza virus vaccine should be avoided or replaced with an alternative during or following atidarsagene autotemcel treatment, as its safety and effectiveness in this context have not been studied. 3. Vaccination is not recommended during the six weeks preceding the start of myeloablative conditioning and should be delayed until hematologic recovery is achieved following treatment. 4. If feasible, childhood vaccinations should be completed before the initiation of myeloablative conditioning. 5. The recombinant quadrivalent influenza virus vaccine should be avoided or replaced with an alternative during or following atidarsagene autotemcel treatment, as its safety and effectiveness remain unstudied. 6. The trivalent influenza virus vaccine should not be used during or following atidarsagene autotemcel treatment due to a lack of safety and efficacy data. 7. The adjuvanted trivalent influenza virus vaccine should also be avoided or replaced with an alternative for the same reasons. 8. The live Japanese encephalitis virus vaccine is not recommended during or following atidarsagene autotemcel treatment, as its safety and effectiveness have not been evaluated. 9. Antiretroviral medications, such as lamivudine, may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. These medications should be discontinued at least one month before cell mobilization or for the expected duration of their elimination. 10. Similarly, maraviroc should be avoided or replaced with an alternative due to potential interference with atidarsagene autotemcel manufacturing. 11. Live vaccines, such as the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine, should not be administered during or following atidarsagene autotemcel treatment. 12. The combined live measles, mumps, rubella, and varicella vaccine is also not recommended for the same reasons. 13. Meningococcal vaccines, including the ACYW polysaccharide-tetanus toxoid conjugate vaccine, should be avoided during or following atidarsagene autotemcel treatment. 14. The meningococcal ACYW-135 diphtheria conjugate vaccine is similarly not recommended. 15. The pentavalent meningococcal ABCWY vaccine should not be used during or following atidarsagene autotemcel treatment. 16. The meningococcal group B vaccine is also not recommended in this context. 17. Pneumococcal vaccines, including the 13-valent, 15-valent, 20-valent, and 21-valent formulations, should be avoided during or following atidarsagene autotemcel treatment. 18. The polyvalent pneumococcal vaccine is similarly not recommended. 19. The inactivated poliovirus vaccine should not be administered during or following atidarsagene autotemcel treatment. 20. Rabies vaccines, including those derived from chick embryo cells, should be avoided during or following atidarsagene autotemcel treatment. 21. Antiretroviral medications, such as nelfinavir, nevirapine, and rilpivirine, may interfere with atidarsagene autotemcel manufacturing and should be discontinued at least one month before cell mobilization or for the expected duration of their elimination. 22. Ritonavir should also be avoided for the same reasons. 23. Live oral rotavirus vaccines should not be administered during or following atidarsagene autotemcel treatment. 24. Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccines, including adjuvanted and mRNA formulations, should be avoided during or following atidarsagene autotemcel treatment. In all cases, the safety and effectiveness of these vaccines or medications during or following atidarsagene autotemcel treatment have not been studied, and their use is not recommended during the six weeks preceding myeloablative conditioning or until hematologic recovery is achieved.
